content.content:
268	## Claude Usage (Usage.cs / ClaudeUsageControl / ClaudeUsageToolWindow)
269	
270	- Tool window: Embeds `claude.ai/settings/usage` in a WebView2 control (`ClaudeUsageToolWindow`, GUID `C3D4E5F6-...`); opened via toolbar or menu
271	- X-button behavior: Intercepted via `IVsWindowFrameNotify2.OnClose` — calls `frame.Hide()` and returns `E_ABORT` so the WebView2 scraper keeps running in the background
272	- `ForceClose()`: Toolbar toggle calls this to fully destroy the window (WebView2 disposed); distinct from X-button hide
273	- Inline usage bars: Mini progress bars in the prompt panel showing session/weekly usage; populated from `UsageSnapshot`; hidden when scraping fails or user not signed in
274	- Snapshot caching: Last successful scrape serialized as JSON to `LastUsageJson` + `LastUsageTimestamp`; restored on startup so bars render immediately with stale data while fresh fetch runs
275	- Off-screen background scraper (issue #133): while the tool window is closed, the WebView2 is parented into a hidden top-level `Window` owned by the VS main window (`ClaudeUsageControl.EnsureOffscreenHost`, positioned at -32000/-32000, `ShowActivated=false`, `ShowInTaskbar=false`, 1024×768 so claude.ai renders its desktop layout) instead of into the tool window frame. Reason: hiding the frame tears down the WebView2's `HwndHost` (issue #131), so a frame-parented scraper can only be rebuilt by making the tab visible — which turned every background refresh into a show-hide cycle that popped the usage tab into view once a minute. `EnsureAliveAsync(offscreen)` rebuilds whenever the live instance sits in the wrong host (HwndHost cannot be reparented); `OnWindowBecameVisible` therefore rebuilds into the frame on an explicit open, and the next background tick rebuilds off-screen after the tab is closed again — one rebuild per visibility change instead of one per refresh. Focus priming is suppressed via `SuppressFocus` (background init, off-screen hosting, or control not on screen) so the invisible window never takes keyboard focus
276	- Auto-refresh: `UsageAutoRefreshSeconds` setting (0 = manual); page reload triggered by the scraper — visible in the tool window when its tab is active, off-screen when it is closed, auto-hidden, or behind another tab. `ClaudeUsageToolWindow.VisibilityChanged` hands polling between the page timer and the background timer on every activation/deactivation; `UsageWindowOpened` is only persisted session-restore intent and must never be used as a live-visibility gate. Off/1m only (v67.0, floor lowered from 2m to 1m in v155.0): the 30s/1m/2m/Off combo (both in the tool window toolbar and the Settings *Usage* tab) collapsed to a single Auto-refresh checkbox meaning 0 (off) or 60 s. Because older releases persisted values below that into JSON, every read path floors a positive value to 60 (`ApplyAutoRefreshSeconds`, `StartUsageBackgroundRefreshTimer`, and the Settings dialog's `origAutoRefresh`) rather than migrating the field, so a legacy value is normalized wherever it enters. The background floor for the "Off" case is also 60 s (inline bars still need a slow refresh when the tab is not active).
277	  - `ClaudeCodeControl.Usage.cs`'s background heartbeat timer (`_usageBackgroundRefreshTimer`) always runs once bars are enabled — never gated on visibility at start time — and self-guards per tick against `_usageToolWindow.IsWindowVisible` (issue #111, two rounds): the *cached* tab-active flag that `ClaudeUsageToolWindow` maintains from `IVsWindowFrameNotify.OnShow`'s `FRAMESHOW_TabActivated`/`TabDeactivated`, not a live `IVsWindowFrame.IsVisible()` COM read. `IsVisible()` reports S_OK for any tool window frame that is merely open, including a tab sitting inactive behind a sibling tab in the same dock group — using it as the tick guard (a regression introduced and then reverted in the same round of fixes) made the background refresh believe the Usage tab was always "visible" whenever it was open anywhere, so the bars only ever updated on an explicit click into that tab.
278	- Session restore: `UsageWindowOpened` persisted; `InitializeUsageMonitoring()` auto-reopens the window and reloads data 2s after solution load
279	- Startup refresh of the inline bars (v159.0): after a VS restart the bars stayed on the cached snapshot for the whole session unless the user clicked into the Claude Usage tab. Several independent causes, all fixed together:
280	  - `ClaudeUsageToolWindow.OnToolWindowCreated` seeded its cached tab-active flag (`_isVisible`) from `IVsWindowFrame.IsVisible()`, which is S_OK for a frame that is merely open — exactly the state VS restores the tab in when a sibling tab in its dock group is the active one. Both background-scrape guards read that flag, so they saw "foreground tab" and never scraped. Seeding (and confirming, in `OnShow`) now goes through `IsFrameOnScreen()` → `IVsWindowFrame.IsOnScreen`, which is false for a tab parked behind a sibling. `FRAMESHOW_TabActivated` is still taken at face value; only `WinShown`/`WinRestored`/`WinMaximized` — which VS also raises for `ShowNoActivate` on an obscured tab — are confirmed against it.
281	  - The WebView2 WPF control only completes `EnsureCoreWebView2Async` once its host window renders, so the in-frame build triggered by restoring that never-rendered tab (`OnWindowBecameVisible` → `ReviveOnShowAsync`) never finished. Every `EnsureAliveAsync` caller awaits the same in-flight `_pendingWebViewInit`, so the off-screen scraper could not be built either — one hung build poisoned usage refresh for the session. `EnsureCoreWebView2WithTimeoutAsync` bounds the wait (30 s) and throws `TimeoutException`, which `InitializeWebViewAsync` handles by discarding the half-built instance *without* the WebView2-runtime error panel (it is not a runtime problem) so the next build starts clean.
282	  - `RefreshUsageInBackgroundAsync` no longer forces `EnsureAliveAsync(offscreen: true)` on an instance that is alive in the frame — that rebuild tears the WebView2 out of the tab it renders in (HwndHost cannot be reparented). A live instance scrapes fine wherever it is parented, so it is `Reload()`ed instead; the off-screen build is the fallback for "nothing alive" plus one retry when a reloaded frame-hosted instance stays silent for 10 s (its rendering host was already gone — issue #131).
283	  - `EnsureUsageToolWindowAsync`'s `showWindow` branch kicks one `RefreshUsageInBackgroundAsync()` when `activate` is false (the startup restore), since a restored-but-unrendered tab never loads its page. The call self-guards on the tab-active flag, so it is a no-op when the tab really is showing.
284	- User-data folder (persistence): A single fixed `%LocalAppData%\ClaudeCodeExtension\WebView2` folder holds the WebView2 profile so cookies/localStorage/IndexedDB survive a VS restart (devenv gets a new PID each launch — the old per-PID folder started every session logged-out, issue #62). `ClaudeUsageWebViewEnvironment.GetOrCreateAsync(primary, fallback)` falls back to a per-PID `WebView2_<pid>` folder only if `CreateAsync` throws because another VS process holds the lock. `CleanupStaleWebView2Folders()` reclaims dead `WebView2_*` folders (glob excludes the fixed `WebView2`). `shared_cookies.json` (`Load/SaveSharedCookiesAsync`) is a DPAPI-protected secondary fallback restore path; legacy plaintext payloads are read once and rewritten protected on the next save
285	- Bar role: `meter` (was `progressbar`) + language-independent parsing (v54.0): Claude.ai's usage page switched the bars from `[role=progressbar]` to `[role=meter]` (inside `data-cds=Meter`) and localizes all labels ("Sessão atual"/"Todos os modelos"/"Fable"). The scraper had queried `[role=progressbar][aria-valuenow]` everywhere, so it found zero bars → `extract()` returned null (inline bars kept showing the stale cached snapshot) and page isolation found no target (full settings page with sidebar rendered instead of the trimmed block). Fixed by matching both roles via the `BAR_SEL`/`BAR_ROLE_SEL`/`isBarRole()` helpers (kept dual so a revert or cached page still parses) across `findSection`, `findIsolationTarget`, `clearStaleInlineWidths` (must skip meter descendants too, or it wipes the inline fill `width:63%`), the trim CSS, and `extract`. Row identification is now language-independent: labels read via `aria-labelledby`→`getElementById` (`readBarLabelAndReset`) with the `.text-primary` column as fallback, session/weekly matched by multi-language keyword regex but ultimately by document order (session = first bar; weekly = the aggregate "all models" bar, which always precedes per-model bars like Fable — so weekly falls back to "first row after session", never a per-model bar). `readUsedPercent` prefers `aria-valuetext` ("63% usado"/"63% used") so extra-usage percent survives localization and the >100% case. The old `div[tabindex=-1].outline-none` isolation target is gone from the page; the bar→`closest('section')`→`parentElement` (`div.pb-8`) fallback now supplies it. Pure JS fix — `UsageSnapshot` field names and the C# side are unchanged
286	- Spend-limit-only pages and stale snapshots (issue #182, v214.0): `extract()` used to return null unless it found *two* rows, and `postSnapshot()` silently drops a null — so a page with a single meter (usage-based Enterprise seats: one monthly spend bar, no session/weekly limits; also any account whose second meter disappears, e.g. an expired included-credit grant that the `r !== sessionRow` fallback had been using as "weekly") never posted again, and the bars showed the cached snapshot forever. The weekly row is now optional: the snapshot carries `NoWeeklyLimit` (negative on purpose, so snapshots cached by older versions deserialize to false and keep their weekly row) and `ApplyUsageSnapshot` collapses `InlineWeeklyStack`/bar/pct when it is set. Separately, `UpdateInlineUsageStaleNotice()` shows a "Not updated since …" line (`InlineUsageStaleNotice`) when `LastUsageTimestamp` is older than `UsageSnapshotStaleAfter` (30 min — a healthy background refresh lands one per minute); evaluated on startup restore, after each scrape, after each background tick and on tab visibility change. Suppressed while the usage tab is the foreground tab, because the page there only posts on change and the timestamp can legitimately age while the data is live.
287	- Fable gated on usage credits (v215.0): Fable needs usage credits, so `extract()` also reads the balance from the header of `#extra-usage-credits-section` (`[data-settings-group-header]` → last child, e.g. `R$0`) into `UsageSnapshot.UsageCreditsBalance` (verbatim). `UsageSnapshot.IsZeroCreditBalance` (pure, unit-tested) is true only when the text has a digit and every digit is zero; `IsFableModelOffered()` reads it from the cached `LastUsageJson`. Fail-open on purpose: no snapshot, no section, no amount, or a snapshot cached by an older version (field absent) all keep Fable offered. Consumers: the 🤖 model menu (`ModelContextMenu_Opened`), both native-chat composer model menus, and the Recommend AI Model dialog picker — each still shows Fable when it is the current pick so the selection has a row; the dialog maps an advisor answer of `fable` to Opus with a note (the advisor schema itself is unchanged).
288	- Returning to the usage view after a manual account switch (v158.0): `TryRedirectToUsage`'s post-auth landing whitelist (`/new`, `/chats`, `/chat/`, `/projects`, `/recents`) deliberately excluded the root path, because `/` doubles as the signed-out home page and redirecting it unconditionally loops `/settings/usage → / → /settings/usage`. claude.ai drops a fresh sign-in on `/` about as often as on `/new`, so Switch Account → native "Log out" → sign in as a different user left the panel parked on the home page until the user pressed Refresh. `_sawSignedOutPage` (set whenever the embedded page visits `/login`, `/logout`, `/magic-link` or `/auth`) now promotes `/` to a landing, and `RedirectToUsageIfSettledAsync` requires a non-empty claude.ai `sessionKey` cookie (`HasClaudeSessionCookieAsync`) before navigating — a genuinely signed-out root reads no cookie and is left alone. The flag is cleared as the redirect fires, so a navigate that bounces straight back to `/` cannot re-arm it: one attempt per sign-out. The settle path re-checks `core.Source` both before and after the awaited cookie read, since the await gives the page another chance to move. `/onboarding` is deliberately *not* a landing — an account claude.ai forces through onboarding would ping-pong `/onboarding → /settings/usage` every ~6.5 s (1.5 s settle + 5 s debounce).
289	- Trim restore after Switch Account (`TryRestoreTrim`, v158.0): `SwitchAccountButton_Click` sets `window.__claudeSuppressTrim` so claude.ai's own chrome — and with it the account menu — stays visible. That flag lives on the document, so a full page load clears it by itself, but an SPA route change back to `/settings/usage` does not, leaving the raw settings page (sidebar and all) in the panel. Both `OnNavigationCompleted` and `OnSourceChanged` now clear the flag whenever the source is on `/settings/usage`, ahead of the redirect check.
290	- Following a Claude CLI account switch (v221.0): the bars come from the WebView2's own claude.ai session, which has nothing to do with the CLI's credentials, so `/logout` + `/login` typed into the terminal (or `claude auth login` anywhere) moved the agent to another account while the bars kept scraping, and refreshing, the old one. Only the ⚙ "Change Account" items signed the page out. `SyncUsageWithClaudeAccountAsync` runs on every background tick (ahead of the foreground-tab guard) and once before the startup refresh. It reads `oauthAccount` from the active side's `~/.claude.json` (the distro's copy for `ClaudeCodeWSL`, with the `wslpath` result cached per session). `CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR` is honored on both sides (`GetClaudeJsonPath`, `${CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR:-$HOME}` under WSL), because the CLI then keeps the file in that folder and never writes the one in the home directory. It identifies the account as `accountUuid/organizationUuid`, so switching organizations under the same login counts as a switch too, since usage limits are per organization. It falls back to the e-mail address when the UUIDs are missing. No `oauthAccount` (between `/logout` and `/login`) or a half-written file reads as "unknown" and never as a switch. The account the page was last paired with is kept per side (`windows`/`wsl`) in `usage-account.json` next to the settings, not in the settings. Every VS window saves its whole in-memory settings on each scrape, so a second window would write the old account back and then sign the shared page out a second time. The first check on a side only records the account. A window can find the pairing already moved to the account it now reads, because another window handled the switch. It then only drops its own cached snapshot (`_usageAccountSeen`), since its bars would otherwise sit on the old numbers until the next successful scrape. A change calls `SignOutUsageWindowIfActiveAsync(pairedAccount)`, which clears the cached snapshot, signs the page out and shows a main-window info bar (`InfoBarSlot.UsageAccount`) with an "Open Claude Usage" link. It deliberately does not pop the tab, which could steal focus while the user types. The Change Account menu items pass no account, which forgets the pairing, so the CLI login that follows is adopted silently instead of being handled as a second switch.
291	  - `SignOutAsync` used to delete cookies only on a live instance. When none was alive (never built this session, torn down with its hidden tab by #131, or a timed-out build), only `shared_cookies.json` went away. The `sessionKey` stayed in the persistent profile, and the next rebuild came straight back as the old account. It now builds an instance first (`_clearProfileOnNextBuild` makes `InitializeWebViewAsync` clear the profile before `LoadSharedCookiesAsync` and the first navigation). It clears with `Profile.ClearBrowsingDataAsync(AllSite)` rather than claude.ai cookies alone, because a "Continue with Google" sign-in keeps its own session in the profile and would silently sign the old account back in. It then navigates to the usage URL, and it resets the cookie-save throttle so the new account's first scrape writes `shared_cookies.json` immediately. `SignOutUsageWindowIfActiveAsync` gets the control through `GetUsageControlAsync`, which creates the hidden tool window when this session has not yet done so.
292	- Corporate proxy interstitial handling (`TryHandleUrlBlock`): Detects when `core.Source` ends with `/urlblock.php` (iboss/Forcepoint/Zscaler style block pages) and injects a JS poller that retries up to 25× at 200ms looking for the Continue submit button — multiple selector fallbacks (`input[type=submit][name=ok]` → generic `input[type=submit]` → `button[type=submit]` → `button[name=ok]` → `form.submit()`). Works while the tool window is hidden because CoreWebView2 processes navigation and JS without a visible rendering surface. Throttled to one click per 3 s. Triggered from both `OnNavigationCompleted` and `OnSourceChanged`
293	- Scrollbox preservation (v73.0): `isolatePath()` used to mark *every* ancestor between the isolation target and `<body>` as `data-claude-usage-path`, whose CSS forces `display:block; height:auto; overflow:visible` — this silently deleted claude.ai's own internal scroll pane (a `flex-1 min-h-0 overflow-y-auto` wrapper around the settings content), so anything below the initial fold (e.g. the Usage Credits spend/balance/buy-credits rows) was unreachable with no scrollbar at all. Fix: while walking up, the first ancestor whose *native* computed `overflow-y` is `auto`/`scroll` (checked before any of our own attributes could affect it) is tagged `data-claude-usage-scrollbox` instead of `-path`; every further ancestor above it is tagged the same way (`pastScrollbox` flag) since they're all part of its flex height-bounding chain. The `scrollbox` CSS rule only strips width caps/grid columns — it never touches `display`/`height`/`overflow`, so the pane's native scrollbar keeps working exactly as it does in a real browser tab.
294	  - Follow-up — the `keep` rule was the same bug (v73.0): the ancestor-side fix alone didn't restore scrolling, because `findIsolationTarget()` can resolve to a `tabindex=-1` dialog shell (not just the small `div.pb-8` block) when the page has one — that shell itself commonly uses `display:flex; flex-direction:column` to stack a header above the internally-scrolling body. The `[data-claude-usage-keep="1"]` rule was still forcing `display:block !important` on the target, which collapses that flex-column and strips the scrollable child's bounded height (its `flex-1`/`min-h-0` become no-ops once the parent isn't a flex container) — the shell's own untouched `overflow:hidden` then just clips the excess with no scrollbar, no matter what the ancestor-side fix does. `keep` now only widens the target (`width`/`max-width`/`margin`/`box-sizing`) and leaves `display`/`height`/`overflow`/`padding` completely alone, same principle as the `scrollbox` rule.
295	- Docked tab painting over its neighbour (v230.0): the WebView2 is a native child window, so WPF clipping and z-order never apply to it. Measured on a tab docked in the document well with the Output pane below: the control's bottom edge landed at the bottom of the Output pane, i.e. it was laid out ~280 px taller than the area the shell shows, so the shell clipped the WPF elements (status bar) while the native window kept painting over Output. `ClaudeUsageControl`'s guard (`#region WebView2 bounds guard`) runs 150 ms after `SizeChanged`/`IsVisibleChanged`/the frame's `OnSize`, and on a 2 s heartbeat while the control is loaded. ## Claude Usage (Usage.cs / ClaudeUsageControl / ClaudeUsageToolWindow)

- Tool window: Embeds `claude.ai/settings/usage` in a WebView2 control (`ClaudeUsageToolWindow`, GUID `C3D4E5F6-...`); opened via toolbar or menu
- X-button behavior: Intercepted via `IVsWindowFrameNotify2.OnClose` — calls `frame.Hide()` and returns `E_ABORT` so the WebView2 scraper keeps running in the background
- `ForceClose()`: Toolbar toggle calls this to fully destroy the window (WebView2 disposed); distinct from X-button hide
- Inline usage bars: Mini progress bars in the prompt panel showing session/weekly usage; populated from `UsageSnapshot`; hidden when scraping fails or user not signed in
- Snapshot caching: Last successful scrape serialized as JSON to `LastUsageJson` + `LastUsageTimestamp`; restored on startup so bars render immediately with stale data while fresh fetch runs
- Off-screen background scraper (issue #133): while the tool window is closed, the WebView2 is parented into a hidden top-level `Window` owned by the VS main window (`ClaudeUsageControl.EnsureOffscreenHost`, positioned at -32000/-32000, `ShowActivated=false`, `ShowInTaskbar=false`, 1024×768 so claude.ai renders its desktop layout) instead of into the tool window frame. Reason: hiding the frame tears down the WebView2's `HwndHost` (issue #131), so a frame-parented scraper can only be rebuilt by making the tab visible — which turned every background refresh into a show-hide cycle that popped the usage tab into view once a minute. `EnsureAliveAsync(offscreen)` rebuilds whenever the live instance sits in the wrong host (HwndHost cannot be reparented); `OnWindowBecameVisible` therefore rebuilds into the frame on an explicit open, and the next background tick rebuilds off-screen after the tab is closed again — one rebuild per visibility change instead of one per refresh. Focus priming is suppressed via `SuppressFocus` (background init, off-screen hosting, or control not on screen) so the invisible window never takes keyboard focus
- Auto-refresh: `UsageAutoRefreshSeconds` setting (0 = manual); page reload triggered by the scraper — visible in the tool window when its tab is active, off-screen when it is closed, auto-hidden, or behind another tab. `ClaudeUsageToolWindow.VisibilityChanged` hands polling between the page timer and the background timer on every activation/deactivation; `UsageWindowOpened` is only persisted session-restore intent and must never be used as a live-visibility gate. Off/1m only (v67.0, floor lowered from 2m to 1m in v155.0): the 30s/1m/2m/Off combo (both in the tool window toolbar and the Settings *Usage* tab) collapsed to a single Auto-refresh checkbox meaning 0 (off) or 60 s. Because older releases persisted values below that into JSON, every read path floors a positive value to 60 (`ApplyAutoRefreshSeconds`, `StartUsageBackgroundRefreshTimer`, and the Settings dialog's `origAutoRefresh`) rather than migrating the field, so a legacy value is normalized wherever it enters. The background floor for the "Off" case is also 60 s (inline bars still need a slow refresh when the tab is not active).
  - `ClaudeCodeControl.Usage.cs`'s background heartbeat timer (`_usageBackgroundRefreshTimer`) always runs once bars are enabled — never gated on visibility at start time — and self-guards per tick against `_usageToolWindow.IsWindowVisible` (issue #111, two rounds): the *cached* tab-active flag that `ClaudeUsageToolWindow` maintains from `IVsWindowFrameNotify.OnShow`'s `FRAMESHOW_TabActivated`/`TabDeactivated`, not a live `IVsWindowFrame.IsVisible()` COM read. `IsVisible()` reports S_OK for any tool window frame that is merely open, including a tab sitting inactive behind a sibling tab in the same dock group — using it as the tick guard (a regression introduced and then reverted in the same round of fixes) made the background refresh believe the Usage tab was always "visible" whenever it was open anywhere, so the bars only ever updated on an explicit click into that tab.
- Session restore: `UsageWindowOpened` persisted; `InitializeUsageMonitoring()` auto-reopens the window and reloads data 2s after solution load
- Startup refresh of the inline bars (v159.0): after a VS restart the bars stayed on the cached snapshot for the whole session unless the user clicked into the Claude Usage tab. Several independent causes, all fixed together:
  - `ClaudeUsageToolWindow.OnToolWindowCreated` seeded its cached tab-active flag (`_isVisible`) from `IVsWindowFrame.IsVisible()`, which is S_OK for a frame that is merely open — exactly the state VS restores the tab in when a sibling tab in its dock group is the active one. Both background-scrape guards read that flag, so they saw "foreground tab" and never scraped. Seeding (and confirming, in `OnShow`) now goes through `IsFrameOnScreen()` → `IVsWindowFrame.IsOnScreen`, which is false for a tab parked behind a sibling. `FRAMESHOW_TabActivated` is still taken at face value; only `WinShown`/`WinRestored`/`WinMaximized` — which VS also raises for `ShowNoActivate` on an obscured tab — are confirmed against it.
  - The WebView2 WPF control only completes `EnsureCoreWebView2Async` once its host window renders, so the in-frame build triggered by restoring that never-rendered tab (`OnWindowBecameVisible` → `ReviveOnShowAsync`) never finished.   - `RefreshUsageInBackgroundAsync` no longer forces `EnsureAliveAsync(offscreen: true)` on an instance that is alive in the frame — that rebuild tears the WebView2 out of the tab it renders in (HwndHost cannot be reparented). Pure JS fix — `UsageSnapshot` field names and the C# side are unchanged

- Fable gated on usage credits (v215.0): Fable needs usage credits, so `extract()` also reads the balance from the header of `#extra-usage-credits-section` (`[data-settings-group-header]` → last child, e.g. `R$0`) into `UsageSnapshot.UsageCreditsBalance` (verbatim). `UsageSnapshot.IsZeroCreditBalance` (pure, unit-tested) is true only when the text has a digit and every digit is zero; `IsFableModelOffered()` reads it from the cached `LastUsageJson`.                     <TextBlock Text="{local:Loc 'Download WebView2 Runtime'}" FontSize="12"/>

                       FontSize="10" Opacity="0.75"
                       Foreground="{DynamicResource {x:Static vsshell:VsBrushes.ToolWindowTextKey}}"/>
        </Border>
    </Grid>
</UserControl>

content.content:
268	## Claude Usage (Usage.cs / ClaudeUsageControl / ClaudeUsageToolWindow)
269	
270	- Tool window: Embeds `claude.ai/settings/usage` in a WebView2 control (`ClaudeUsageToolWindow`, GUID `C3D4E5F6-...`); opened via toolbar or menu
271	- X-button behavior: Intercepted via `IVsWindowFrameNotify2.OnClose` — calls `frame.Hide()` and returns `E_ABORT` so the WebView2 scraper keeps running in the background
272	- `ForceClose()`: Toolbar toggle calls this to fully destroy the window (WebView2 disposed); distinct from X-button hide
273	- Inline usage bars: Mini progress bars in the prompt panel showing session/weekly usage; populated from `UsageSnapshot`; hidden when scraping fails or user not signed in
274	- Snapshot caching: Last successful scrape serialized as JSON to `LastUsageJson` + `LastUsageTimestamp`; restored on startup so bars render immediately with stale data while fresh fetch runs
275	- Off-screen background scraper (issue #133): while the tool window is closed, the WebView2 is parented into a hidden top-level `Window` owned by the VS main window (`ClaudeUsageControl.EnsureOffscreenHost`, positioned at -32000/-32000, `ShowActivated=false`, `ShowInTaskbar=false`, 1024×768 so claude.ai renders its desktop layout) instead of into the tool window frame. Reason: hiding the frame tears down the WebView2's `HwndHost` (issue #131), so a frame-parented scraper can only be rebuilt by making the tab visible — which turned every background refresh into a show-hide cycle that popped the usage tab into view once a minute. `EnsureAliveAsync(offscreen)` rebuilds whenever the live instance sits in the wrong host (HwndHost cannot be reparented); `OnWindowBecameVisible` therefore rebuilds into the frame on an explicit open, and the next background tick rebuilds off-screen after the tab is closed again — one rebuild per visibility change instead of one per refresh. Focus priming is suppressed via `SuppressFocus` (background init, off-screen hosting, or control not on screen) so the invisible window never takes keyboard focus
276	- Auto-refresh: `UsageAutoRefreshSeconds` setting (0 = manual); page reload triggered by the scraper — visible in the tool window when its tab is active, off-screen when it is closed, auto-hidden, or behind another tab. `ClaudeUsageToolWindow.VisibilityChanged` hands polling between the page timer and the background timer on every activation/deactivation; `UsageWindowOpened` is only persisted session-restore intent and must never be used as a live-visibility gate. Off/1m only (v67.0, floor lowered from 2m to 1m in v155.0): the 30s/1m/2m/Off combo (both in the tool window toolbar and the Settings *Usage* tab) collapsed to a single Auto-refresh checkbox meaning 0 (off) or 60 s. Because older releases persisted values below that into JSON, every read path floors a positive value to 60 (`ApplyAutoRefreshSeconds`, `StartUsageBackgroundRefreshTimer`, and the Settings dialog's `origAutoRefresh`) rather than migrating the field, so a legacy value is normalized wherever it enters. The background floor for the "Off" case is also 60 s (inline bars still need a slow refresh when the tab is not active).
277	  - `ClaudeCodeControl.Usage.cs`'s background heartbeat timer (`_usageBackgroundRefreshTimer`) always runs once bars are enabled — never gated on visibility at start time — and self-guards per tick against `_usageToolWindow.IsWindowVisible` (issue #111, two rounds): the *cached* tab-active flag that `ClaudeUsageToolWindow` maintains from `IVsWindowFrameNotify.OnShow`'s `FRAMESHOW_TabActivated`/`TabDeactivated`, not a live `IVsWindowFrame.IsVisible()` COM read. `IsVisible()` reports S_OK for any tool window frame that is merely open, including a tab sitting inactive behind a sibling tab in the same dock group — using it as the tick guard (a regression introduced and then reverted in the same round of fixes) made the background refresh believe the Usage tab was always "visible" whenever it was open anywhere, so the bars only ever updated on an explicit click into that tab.
278	- Session restore: `UsageWindowOpened` persisted; `InitializeUsageMonitoring()` auto-reopens the window and reloads data 2s after solution load
279	- Startup refresh of the inline bars (v159.0): after a VS restart the bars stayed on the cached snapshot for the whole session unless the user clicked into the Claude Usage tab. Several independent causes, all fixed together:
280	  - `ClaudeUsageToolWindow.OnToolWindowCreated` seeded its cached tab-active flag (`_isVisible`) from `IVsWindowFrame.IsVisible()`, which is S_OK for a frame that is merely open — exactly the state VS restores the tab in when a sibling tab in its dock group is the active one. Both background-scrape guards read that flag, so they saw "foreground tab" and never scraped. Seeding (and confirming, in `OnShow`) now goes through `IsFrameOnScreen()` → `IVsWindowFrame.IsOnScreen`, which is false for a tab parked behind a sibling. `FRAMESHOW_TabActivated` is still taken at face value; only `WinShown`/`WinRestored`/`WinMaximized` — which VS also raises for `ShowNoActivate` on an obscured tab — are confirmed against it.
281	  - The WebView2 WPF control only completes `EnsureCoreWebView2Async` once its host window renders, so the in-frame build triggered by restoring that never-rendered tab (`OnWindowBecameVisible` → `ReviveOnShowAsync`) never finished. Every `EnsureAliveAsync` caller awaits the same in-flight `_pendingWebViewInit`, so the off-screen scraper could not be built either — one hung build poisoned usage refresh for the session. `EnsureCoreWebView2WithTimeoutAsync` bounds the wait (30 s) and throws `TimeoutException`, which `InitializeWebViewAsync` handles by discarding the half-built instance *without* the WebView2-runtime error panel (it is not a runtime problem) so the next build starts clean.
282	  - `RefreshUsageInBackgroundAsync` no longer forces `EnsureAliveAsync(offscreen: true)` on an instance that is alive in the frame — that rebuild tears the WebView2 out of the tab it renders in (HwndHost cannot be reparented). A live instance scrapes fine wherever it is parented, so it is `Reload()`ed instead; the off-screen build is the fallback for "nothing alive" plus one retry when a reloaded frame-hosted instance stays silent for 10 s (its rendering host was already gone — issue #131).
283	  - `EnsureUsageToolWindowAsync`'s `showWindow` branch kicks one `RefreshUsageInBackgroundAsync()` when `activate` is false (the startup restore), since a restored-but-unrendered tab never loads its page. The call self-guards on the tab-active flag, so it is a no-op when the tab really is showing.
284	- User-data folder (persistence): A single fixed `%LocalAppData%\ClaudeCodeExtension\WebView2` folder holds the WebView2 profile so cookies/localStorage/IndexedDB survive a VS restart (devenv gets a new PID each launch — the old per-PID folder started every session logged-out, issue #62). `ClaudeUsageWebViewEnvironment.GetOrCreateAsync(primary, fallback)` falls back to a per-PID `WebView2_<pid>` folder only if `CreateAsync` throws because another VS process holds the lock. `CleanupStaleWebView2Folders()` reclaims dead `WebView2_*` folders (glob excludes the fixed `WebView2`). `shared_cookies.json` (`Load/SaveSharedCookiesAsync`) is a DPAPI-protected secondary fallback restore path; legacy plaintext payloads are read once and rewritten protected on the next save
285	- Bar role: `meter` (was `progressbar`) + language-independent parsing (v54.0): Claude.ai's usage page switched the bars from `[role=progressbar]` to `[role=meter]` (inside `data-cds=Meter`) and localizes all labels ("Sessão atual"/"Todos os modelos"/"Fable"). The scraper had queried `[role=progressbar][aria-valuenow]` everywhere, so it found zero bars → `extract()` returned null (inline bars kept showing the stale cached snapshot) and page isolation found no target (full settings page with sidebar rendered instead of the trimmed block). Fixed by matching both roles via the `BAR_SEL`/`BAR_ROLE_SEL`/`isBarRole()` helpers (kept dual so a revert or cached page still parses) across `findSection`, `findIsolationTarget`, `clearStaleInlineWidths` (must skip meter descendants too, or it wipes the inline fill `width:63%`), the trim CSS, and `extract`. Row identification is now language-independent: labels read via `aria-labelledby`→`getElementById` (`readBarLabelAndReset`) with the `.text-primary` column as fallback, session/weekly matched by multi-language keyword regex but ultimately by document order (session = first bar; weekly = the aggregate "all models" bar, which always precedes per-model bars like Fable — so weekly falls back to "first row after session", never a per-model bar). `readUsedPercent` prefers `aria-valuetext` ("63% usado"/"63% used") so extra-usage percent survives localization and the >100% case. The old `div[tabindex=-1].outline-none` isolation target is gone from the page; the bar→`closest('section')`→`parentElement` (`div.pb-8`) fallback now supplies it. Pure JS fix — `UsageSnapshot` field names and the C# side are unchanged
286	- Spend-limit-only pages and stale snapshots (issue #182, v214.0): `extract()` used to return null unless it found *two* rows, and `postSnapshot()` silently drops a null — so a page with a single meter (usage-based Enterprise seats: one monthly spend bar, no session/weekly limits; also any account whose second meter disappears, e.g. an expired included-credit grant that the `r !== sessionRow` fallback had been using as "weekly") never posted again, and the bars showed the cached snapshot forever. The weekly row is now optional: the snapshot carries `NoWeeklyLimit` (negative on purpose, so snapshots cached by older versions deserialize to false and keep their weekly row) and `ApplyUsageSnapshot` collapses `InlineWeeklyStack`/bar/pct when it is set. Separately, `UpdateInlineUsageStaleNotice()` shows a "Not updated since …" line (`InlineUsageStaleNotice`) when `LastUsageTimestamp` is older than `UsageSnapshotStaleAfter` (30 min — a healthy background refresh lands one per minute); evaluated on startup restore, after each scrape, after each background tick and on tab visibility change. Suppressed while the usage tab is the foreground tab, because the page there only posts on change and the timestamp can legitimately age while the data is live.
287	- Fable gated on usage credits (v215.0): Fable needs usage credits, so `extract()` also reads the balance from the header of `#extra-usage-credits-section` (`[data-settings-group-header]` → last child, e.g. `R$0`) into `UsageSnapshot.UsageCreditsBalance` (verbatim). `UsageSnapshot.IsZeroCreditBalance` (pure, unit-tested) is true only when the text has a digit and every digit is zero; `IsFableModelOffered()` reads it from the cached `LastUsageJson`. Fail-open on purpose: no snapshot, no section, no amount, or a snapshot cached by an older version (field absent) all keep Fable offered. Consumers: the 🤖 model menu (`ModelContextMenu_Opened`), both native-chat composer model menus, and the Recommend AI Model dialog picker — each still shows Fable when it is the current pick so the selection has a row; the dialog maps an advisor answer of `fable` to Opus with a note (the advisor schema itself is unchanged).

        /// <summary>
        /// Shows the ring and fills the popup. The ring fills with the context window in use, or with the
        /// session limit when no turn has reported a context window yet. Null or not visible hides the button.
        /// </summary>
        public void SetUsageIndicator(ChatUsageIndicatorData data)
        {
            bool visible = data != null && data.Visible;
            Visibility previous = ComposerUsageButton.Visibility;
            ComposerUsageButton.Visibility = visible ? Visibility.Visible : Visibility.Collapsed;
            if (previous != ComposerUsageButton.Visibility)
            {
                RefreshComposerDensity();
            }

            if (!visible)
            {
                UsagePopup.IsOpen = false;
                ComposerUsageRingArc.Data = null;
                return;
            }

            int ringPercent = data.HasContext
                ? ChatUsageIndicator.ClampPercent(data.ContextPercent)
                : data.HasPlanUsage ? ChatUsageIndicator.ClampPercent(data.SessionPercent) : -1;
            ComposerUsageRingArc.Data = ringPercent < 0
                ? null
                : ChatUsageIndicator.RingArc(ringPercent / 100.0, 7, 6);
            ComposerUsageButton.ToolTip = ringPercent < 0
                ? L("Usage: context window and plan limits")
                : L("Usage: {0}% used", ringPercent);

            UsageContextText.Text = data.HasContext
                ? ChatUsageIndicator.ContextLine(data.ContextTokens, data.ContextWindow)
                : L("No turn yet");
            UsageContextBar.Value = data.HasContext ? ChatUsageIndicator.ClampPercent(data.ContextPercent) : 0;

            UsageNoPlanText.Visibility = data.HasPlanUsage ? Visibility.Collapsed : Visibility.Visible;
            UsagePlanRows.Visibility = data.HasPlanUsage ? Visibility.Visible : Visibility.Collapsed;
            if (data.HasPlanUsage)
            {
                UsageSessionLabel.Text = string.IsNullOrEmpty(data.SessionLabel) ? L("Session limit") : data.SessionLabel;
                SetPlanRow(UsageSessionText, UsageSessionBar, data.SessionPercent, true, data.SessionReset);

                SetPlanRow(UsageWeeklyText, UsageWeeklyBar, data.WeeklyPercent, data.ShowWeekly, data.WeeklyReset);
                UsageWeeklyRow.Visibility = data.ShowWeekly ? Visibility.Visible : Visibility.Collapsed;

                SetPlanRow(UsageExtraText, UsageExtraBar, data.ExtraPercent, data.ShowExtra, data.ExtraSpent, data.ExtraReset);
                UsageExtraRow.Visibility = data.ShowExtra ? Visibility.Visible : Visibility.Collapsed;
            }

            _usageUpdatedText = data.UpdatedText ?? string.Empty;
            ShowUsageUpdatedText();
        }

## OpenPets

OpenPets MCP tools may be available.

Use OpenPets as a short visible status channel for meaningful coding progress:
- Use `openpets_say` when starting, completing, blocking, or needing review on non-trivial work.
- Keep messages brief, user-facing, and non-sensitive.
- Do not include code, logs, secrets, URLs, or file paths.
- Use `openpets_react` for small visual or emotional feedback.
- Use `openpets_status` only when checking availability or the targeted pet.
- Do not spam every internal step.

# CLAUDE.md - Claude Code Extension for Visual Studio

## Project Overview

Visual Studio Extension (VSIX) for VS 2022/2026 — integrates AI code assistants (Claude Code, OpenAI Codex, Cursor Agent, Open Code, Devin, PI, Google Antigravity, Reasonix, Qwen Code, and Grok) via a native chat tab driven by each CLI's headless protocol ("native mode", default since v179.0) or an embedded terminal (Win32 `SetParent` interop).

- Author: Daniel Carvalho Liedke (dliedke@gmail.com) | License: MIT
- Repository: https://github.com/dliedke/ClaudeCodeExtension
- Current Version: 290.0 | Target Framework: .NET Framework 4.7.2

Step-by-step procedures for recurring tasks (release, Exp-hive debugging, publish, adding a
provider/setting/UI file) live in `docs/SKILLS.md`. Short build/style brief for non-Claude agents: `docs/AGENTS.md`.

---

## MANDATORY: Version & Documentation Updates

Every development session that modifies code MUST update before finishing:

Versioning scheme (since 11.0): each release bumps the MAJOR version by one — 22.0 → 23.0 → 24.0 and so on. Always use `.0` as the minor (AssemblyVersion `24.0.0.0`, manifest `24.0`, README `### Version 24.0`). Do not resume 10.x-style minor bumps.

1. `Properties/AssemblyInfo.cs`: Bump `AssemblyVersion` and `AssemblyFileVersion`
2. `source.extension.vsixmanifest`: Bump `Version` in `<Identity>` tag
3. `README.md`: Add `### Version X.Y` entry at top of `## Version History`
   - Style: Short, business-focused. One sentence per bullet (two max). Describe the user-visible feature or fix, not the implementation.
   - Avoid: code/file/class/method names, internal selectors, file paths, constants, line numbers, JS snippets, framework jargon (`CoreWebView2`, `INPUT_RECORD`, `NavigationCompleted`, etc.), step-by-step "how it works" explanations, and PR-description-style root-cause analysis.
   - Keep: what the user gets ("auto-confirms proxy block screens"), opt-in/opt-out status, and the menu/setting name they interact with.
   - Technical details belong in commit messages and `docs/ARCHITECTURE.md`, not in release notes.
   - Merging a contributor PR: besides the "Thanks to [@login](https://github.com/login) for this release (#N)." line in the version entry, update the author's PR count in README's `## Thank You, Contributors` list (add a `1 PR` row for a first-time contributor). Keep the list sorted by PR count descending, ties alphabetical (case-insensitive); the owner `dliedke` is not listed. Counts include every PR the author opened (open, closed or merged) — recount with `gh pr list --state all --limit 1000 --json author`.
   - Other README sections (Features, Supported AI Providers, System Requirements, Settings & Menus, etc.): Edits MUST be minimal. Update only the exact line/bullet affected by the change. Do not rewrite paragraphs, expand explanations, add subsections, reorder content, or restructure tables. If a new provider/setting needs a row, add one row. If a feature description needs a word change, change the word. README is reference doc — keep it slim to avoid file bloat.

---

## Build & Test

```bash
# Release
'/c/Program Files/Microsoft Visual Studio/18/Enterprise/MSBuild/Current/Bin/MSBuild.exe' ClaudeCodeExtension.sln -p:Configuration=Release -v:minimal

# Debug
'/c/Program Files/Microsoft Visual Studio/18/Enterprise/MSBuild/Current/Bin/MSBuild.exe' ClaudeCodeExtension.sln -p:Configuration=Debug -v:minimal
```

- F5 / Ctrl+F5 in Visual Studio → experimental instance with `/rootsuffix Exp`, for Debug and Release

### Debugging in the Exp hive (`deploy-exp.cmd`)

The VSSDK targets default `DeployExtension` to false, so the csproj sets `VSSDKTargetPlatformRegRootSuffix=Exp` and turns `DeployExtension` on for any configuration built inside Visual Studio. Without those two properties F5 opens an Exp instance with no extension in it. Command-line builds (`test.cmd`, `publish.cmd`) keep the default and deploy nothing.

```bash
./deploy-exp.cmd            # build Debug + deploy to the Exp hive
./deploy-exp.cmd -release   # build Release instead of Debug
./deploy-exp.cmd -run       # the above, then start devenv /rootsuffix Exp with the solution
./deploy-exp.cmd -run -open <path.sln>   # start Exp with another solution (e.g. a demo app, so F5 debugs it)
```

- Close the Exp instance before deploying — otherwise it keeps running the previous build.
- A first deploy into a hive that never had the extension fails with `VSSDK1031 ... could not be found`; the script recovers by running `devenv /rootsuffix Exp /updateconfiguration` and retrying.
- The same VSSDK1031 (in VS or from the script) appears when an idle 32-bit MSBuild node from an earlier VS build still holds the Exp hive's `privateregistry.bin` open — `/updateconfiguration` then silently merges nothing. The script ends those nodes before each attempt; inside VS, kill the `MSBuild.exe ... /nodemode:2` process and rebuild.
- Each deploy lands in a version-named folder, so a version bump leaves the previous one behind and the hive can keep loading the older assembly with no error anywhere. The `RemoveStaleExpDeployments` target in the csproj deletes the sibling version folders after every deploy to prevent that.

### Tests (`test.cmd`)

```bash
./test.cmd    # build Tests/ + run the unit suite (seconds, no VS)
```

- Runs `Tests/ClaudeCodeExtension.Tests.csproj` under `vstest.console.exe`: version/package guards (the Newtonsoft pin that would have caught #112, version consistency across the three sources) plus unit tests of the pure helpers.
- `publish.cmd` calls `test.cmd` before the Release rebuild. `SKIP_TESTS=1` bypasses the gate.
- The test project is in the solution without a `Release|Any CPU.Build.0` entry, so the Release rebuild in `publish.cmd` does not build it.
- Everything that needs a running Visual Studio (terminal embedding, provider round-trip, settings dialog) is tested manually with F5.

### Publishing

When the user asks to publish the app (or any equivalent phrasing like "publish the extension", "publish to marketplace", "ship it"), run `publish.cmd` from the repo root. Do not invoke MSBuild or marketplace APIs manually — `publish.cmd` is the authoritative deployment automation.

`publish.cmd` performs: Clean → Rebuild Release → publish VSIX via `VsixPublisher.exe` with `publishManifest.json`. Falls back from VS 2026 to VS 2022 tool paths automatically. Uses `VsixPub0038` log marker to detect success (works around VsixPublisher telemetry crash in VS 18).

`publishManifest.json`: Marketplace metadata — publisher `dliedke`, category `coding`, free, Q&A enabled, README.md as overview.

---

## Architecture — Key Non-Obvious Details

Deep per-file gotchas and design decisions live in `docs/ARCHITECTURE.md` (kept out of this
always-loaded file to keep context lean). Before editing any file below, read its section in that
doc — it captures non-obvious behavior that isn't apparent from the code:

Five cross-cutting rules (full text in `docs/ARCHITECTURE.md` → *Cross-Cutting Rules*) — read before touching provider selection, UI captions, terminal focus, anything that sends text to the agent, or a value chosen for performance:
- Active provider UI rule (v24.0): provider-dependent UI (checkmarks, captions, menu visibility, active labels) must use `_currentRunningProvider` when a terminal is alive, falling back to `_settings.SelectedProvider` only before launch.
- Terminal focus rule (v26.0): never focus the embedded terminal with direct `SetForegroundWindow`/`SetFocus`; use `FocusTerminalForInputAsync()`/`FocusTerminalForInput()`/`FocusTerminalWindow()`. Hook focus checks stay Win32-only.
- Agent send rule (v82.0): send agent-bound text through `SendTextToAgentAsync()`, not `SendTextToTerminalAsync()` — native mode has no console. Console-only traffic (slash commands, CLI updates, plugin installs) is the exception; new console-scraping logic must bail out when `IsNativeModeActive`.
- Chat localization rule (v269.0, whole extension since v270.0): new or changed UI text — chat, panel, menus, dialogs, message boxes — is wrapped in `L("...")`/`N("...")`/`{local:Loc '...'}` and translated in every `lang/*.json` in the same change (recipe: `docs/SKILLS.md` → *Localize chat text*); `test.cmd` fails on a missing or orphaned translation. Text set from code must also be redone by `RefreshChatLanguage()` (or a tool window's own `Loc.LanguageChanged` handler) so a language switch reaches everything already open.
- Performance values rule (v279.0): the resumed-transcript limits and any other value chosen for performance (throttle intervals, virtualization cache, rendering caps) change only together with a measurement recorded in `docs/PERFORMANCE.md` (method, machine, before/after); `ReplayLimitsMatchTheMeasuredValues` pins the limits.

# CLAUDE.md - Claude Code Extension for Visual Studio

## Project Overview

Visual Studio Extension (VSIX) for VS 2022/2026 — integrates AI code assistants (Claude Code, OpenAI Codex, Cursor Agent, Open Code, Devin, PI, Google Antigravity, Reasonix, Qwen Code, and Grok) via a native chat tab driven by each CLI's headless protocol ("native mode", default since v179.0) or an embedded terminal (Win32 `SetParent` interop).

- Author: Daniel Carvalho Liedke (dliedke@gmail.com) | License: MIT
- Repository: https://github.com/dliedke/ClaudeCodeExtension
- Current Version: 290.0 | Target Framework: .NET Framework 4.7.2

Step-by-step procedures for recurring tasks (release, Exp-hive debugging, publish, adding a
provider/setting/UI file) live in `docs/SKILLS.md`. Short build/style brief for non-Claude agents: `docs/AGENTS.md`.

---

## MANDATORY: Version & Documentation Updates

Every development session that modifies code MUST update before finishing:

Versioning scheme (since 11.0): each release bumps the MAJOR version by one — 22.0 → 23.0 → 24.0 and so on. Always use `.0` as the minor (AssemblyVersion `24.0.0.0`, manifest `24.0`, README `### Version 24.0`). Do not resume 10.x-style minor bumps.

1. `Properties/AssemblyInfo.cs`: Bump `AssemblyVersion` and `AssemblyFileVersion`
2. `source.extension.vsixmanifest`: Bump `Version` in `<Identity>` tag
3. `README.md`: Add `### Version X.Y` entry at top of `## Version History`
   - Style: Short, business-focused. One sentence per bullet (two max). Describe the user-visible feature or fix, not the implementation.
   - Avoid: code/file/class/method names, internal selectors, file paths, constants, line numbers, JS snippets, framework jargon (`CoreWebView2`, `INPUT_RECORD`, `NavigationCompleted`, etc.), step-by-step "how it works" explanations, and PR-description-style root-cause analysis.
   - Keep: what the user gets ("auto-confirms proxy block screens"), opt-in/opt-out status, and the menu/setting name they interact with.
   - Technical details belong in commit messages and `docs/ARCHITECTURE.md`, not in release notes.
   - Merging a contributor PR: besides the "Thanks to [@login](https://github.com/login) for this release (#N)." line in the version entry, update the author's PR count in README's `## Thank You, Contributors` list (add a `1 PR` row for a first-time contributor). Keep the list sorted by PR count descending, ties alphabetical (case-insensitive); the owner `dliedke` is not listed. Counts include every PR the author opened (open, closed or merged) — recount with `gh pr list --state all --limit 1000 --json author`.
   - Other README sections (Features, Supported AI Providers, System Requirements, Settings & Menus, etc.): Edits MUST be minimal. Update only the exact line/bullet affected by the change. Do not rewrite paragraphs, expand explanations, add subsections, reorder content, or restructure tables. If a new provider/setting needs a row, add one row. If a feature description needs a word change, change the word. README is reference doc — keep it slim to avoid file bloat.

## Build & Test

```bash
# Release
'/c/Program Files/Microsoft Visual Studio/18/Enterprise/MSBuild/Current/Bin/MSBuild.exe' ClaudeCodeExtension.sln -p:Configuration=Release -v:minimal

# Debug
'/c/Program Files/Microsoft Visual Studio/18/Enterprise/MSBuild/Current/Bin/MSBuild.exe' ClaudeCodeExtension.sln -p:Configuration=Debug -v:minimal
```

- F5 / Ctrl+F5 in Visual Studio → experimental instance with `/rootsuffix Exp`, for Debug and Release

### Debugging in the Exp hive (`deploy-exp.cmd`)

The VSSDK targets default `DeployExtension` to false, so the csproj sets `VSSDKTargetPlatformRegRootSuffix=Exp` and turns `DeployExtension` on for any configuration built inside Visual Studio. Without those two properties F5 opens an Exp instance with no extension in it. Command-line builds (`test.cmd`, `publish.cmd`) keep the default and deploy nothing.

```bash
./deploy-exp.cmd            # build Debug + deploy to the Exp hive
./deploy-exp.cmd -release   # build Release instead of Debug
./deploy-exp.cmd -run       # the above, then start devenv /rootsuffix Exp with the solution
./deploy-exp.cmd -run -open <path.sln>   # start Exp with another solution (e.g. a demo app, so F5 debugs it)
```

- Close the Exp instance before deploying — otherwise it keeps running the previous build.
- A first deploy into a hive that never had the extension fails with `VSSDK1031 ... could not be found`; the script recovers by running `devenv /rootsuffix Exp /updateconfiguration` and retrying.
- The same VSSDK1031 (in VS or from the script) appears when an idle 32-bit MSBuild node from an earlier VS build still holds the Exp hive's `privateregistry.bin` open — `/updateconfiguration` then silently merges nothing. The script ends those nodes before each attempt; inside VS, kill the `MSBuild.exe ... /nodemode:2` process and rebuild.
- Each deploy lands in a version-named folder, so a version bump leaves the previous one behind and the hive can keep loading the older assembly with no error anywhere. The `RemoveStaleExpDeployments` target in the csproj deletes the sibling version folders after every deploy to prevent that.

### Tests (`test.cmd`)

```bash
./test.cmd    # build Tests/ + run the unit suite (seconds, no VS)
```

- Runs `Tests/ClaudeCodeExtension.Tests.csproj` under `vstest.console.exe`: version/package guards (the Newtonsoft pin that would have caught #112, version consistency across the three sources) plus unit tests of the pure helpers.
- `publish.cmd` calls `test.cmd` before the Release rebuild. `SKIP_TESTS=1` bypasses the gate.
- The test project is in the solution without a `Release|Any CPU.Build.0` entry, so the Release rebuild in `publish.cmd` does not build it.
- Everything that needs a running Visual Studio (terminal embedding, provider round-trip, settings dialog) is tested manually with F5.

### Publishing

When the user asks to publish the app (or any equivalent phrasing like "publish the extension", "publish to marketplace", "ship it"), run `publish.cmd` from the repo root. Do not invoke MSBuild or marketplace APIs manually — `publish.cmd` is the authoritative deployment automation.

`publish.cmd` performs: Clean → Rebuild Release → publish VSIX via `VsixPublisher.exe` with `publishManifest.json`. Falls back from VS 2026 to VS 2022 tool paths automatically. Uses `VsixPub0038` log marker to detect success (works around VsixPublisher telemetry crash in VS 18).

`publishManifest.json`: Marketplace metadata — publisher `dliedke`, category `coding`, free, Q&A enabled, README.md as overview.

## Architecture — Key Non-Obvious Details

Deep per-file gotchas and design decisions live in `docs/ARCHITECTURE.md` (kept out of this
always-loaded file to keep context lean). Before editing any file below, read its section in that
doc — it captures non-obvious behavior that isn't apparent from the code:

Five cross-cutting rules (full text in `docs/ARCHITECTURE.md` → *Cross-Cutting Rules*) — read before touching provider selection, UI captions, terminal focus, anything that sends text to the agent, or a value chosen for performance:
- Active provider UI rule (v24.0): provider-dependent UI (checkmarks, captions, menu visibility, active labels) must use `_currentRunningProvider` when a terminal is alive, falling back to `_settings.SelectedProvider` only before launch.
- Terminal focus rule (v26.0): never focus the embedded terminal with direct `SetForegroundWindow`/`SetFocus`; use `FocusTerminalForInputAsync()`/`FocusTerminalForInput()`/`FocusTerminalWindow()`. Hook focus checks stay Win32-only.
- Agent send rule (v82.0): send agent-bound text through `SendTextToAgentAsync()`, not `SendTextToTerminalAsync()` — native mode has no console. Console-only traffic (slash commands, CLI updates, plugin installs) is the exception; new console-scraping logic must bail out when `IsNativeModeActive`.
- Chat localization rule (v269.0, whole extension since v270.0): new or changed UI text — chat, panel, menus, dialogs, message boxes — is wrapped in `L("...")`/`N("...")`/`{local:Loc '...'}` and translated in every `lang/*.json` in the same change (recipe: `docs/SKILLS.md` → *Localize chat text*); `test.cmd` fails on a missing or orphaned translation. Text set from code must also be redone by `RefreshChatLanguage()` (or a tool window's own `Loc.LanguageChanged` handler) so a language switch reaches everything already open.
- Performance values rule (v279.0): the resumed-transcript limits and any other value chosen for performance (throttle intervals, virtualization cache, rendering caps) change only together with a measurement recorded in `docs/PERFORMANCE.md` (method, machine, before/after); `ReplayLimitsMatchTheMeasuredValues` pins the limits.

56	    /// <summary>Pure formatting and geometry behind the usage button; no WPF elements are created here.</summary>
57	    public static class ChatUsageIndicator
58	    {
59	        /// <summary>"413.9k", "1M", "1.2M", "950" — the figures the status line gives, shortened the way the CLI shows them.</summary>
60	        public static string FormatTokens(long tokens)
61	        {
62	            if (tokens < 0) tokens = 0;
63	
64	            // From 999,950 up the thousands would round to "1000k", so the million unit takes over there.
65	            if (tokens >= 999950)
66	            {
67	                return Math.Round(tokens / 1000000.0, 1).ToString("0.#", CultureInfo.InvariantCulture) + "M";
68	            }
69	
70	            if (tokens >= 1000)
71	            {
72	                return Math.Round(tokens / 1000.0, 1).ToString("0.#", CultureInfo.InvariantCulture) + "k";
73	            }
74	
75	            return tokens.ToString(CultureInfo.InvariantCulture);
76	        }
77	
78	        /// <summary>Share of the window in use, 0-100. Input-side tokens only, as the CLI computes it. 0 when the window is unknown.</summary>
79	        public static int ContextPercent(long tokens, int window)
80	        {
81	            if (window <= 0 || tokens <= 0) return 0;
82	
83	            double percent = Math.Min(100.0, tokens * 100.0 / window);
84	            return (int)Math.Round(percent, MidpointRounding.AwayFromZero);
85	        }
86	
87	        /// <summary>"413.9k / 1M (41%)"; just the token count when the window size is unknown.</summary>
88	        public static string ContextLine(long tokens, int window)
89	        {
90	            if (window <= 0)
91	            {
92	                return FormatTokens(tokens);
93	            }
94	
95	            return FormatTokens(tokens) + " / " + FormatTokens(window) + " (" + ContextPercent(tokens, window) + "%)";
96	        }
97	
98	        /// <summary>Clamps a percentage to 0-100 (the usage page can report more for extra usage, which has its own bar).</summary>
99	        public static int ClampPercent(int value)
100	        {
101	            return value < 0 ? 0 : (value > 100 ? 100 : value);
102	        }
103	
104	        /// <summary>"41% used · Resets in 2 h"; blank details are skipped, so a missing reset leaves just the percentage.</summary>
105	        public static string PlanRowText(int percent, params string[] details)
106	        {
107	            string text = Loc.L("{0}% used", ClampPercent(percent));
108	            if (details == null)
109	            {
110	                return text;
111	            }
112	
113	            foreach (string detail in details)
114	            {
115	                string clean = StripIconGlyphs(detail).Trim();
116	                if (clean.Length > 0)
117	                {
118	                    text += " · " + clean;
119	                }
120	            }
121	
122	            return text;
123	        }
124	
125	        /// <summary>
126	        /// Drops Private Use Area characters: claude.ai draws some icons with an icon font, and a snapshot
127	        /// scraped before the page filter existed can hold one where the reset text belongs (a box in VS).
128	        /// </summary>
129	        public static string StripIconGlyphs(string text)
130	        {
131	            if (string.IsNullOrEmpty(text))
132	            {
133	                return string.Empty;
134	            }
135	
136	            var sb = new StringBuilder(text.Length);
137	            foreach (char c in text)
138	            {
139	                if (c < '' || c > '')
140	                {
141	                    sb.Append(c);
142	                }
143	            }
144	
145	            return sb.ToString();
146	        }

148	        /// <summary>
149	        /// The ring's arc for <paramref name="fraction"/> (0-1) of a circle centred on
150	        /// (<paramref name="center"/>, <paramref name="center"/>), starting at 12 o'clock and running clockwise.
151	        /// Null when there is nothing to draw. A full circle stops just short of closing: an arc whose start and
152	        /// end coincide is not drawn at all.
153	        /// </summary>
154	        public static PathGeometry RingArc(double fraction, double center, double radius)
155	        {
156	            if (double.IsNaN(fraction) || fraction <= 0) return null;
157	
158	            double sweep = Math.Min(fraction, 0.9999);
159	            var figure = new PathFigure
160	            {
161	                StartPoint = new Point(center, center - radius),
162	                IsClosed = false
163	            };
164	            figure.Segments.Add(new ArcSegment(
165	                ArcPoint(sweep, center, radius),
166	                new Size(radius, radius),
167	                0,
168	                sweep > 0.5,
169	                SweepDirection.Clockwise,
170	                true));
171	
172	            var geometry = new PathGeometry();
173	            geometry.Figures.Add(figure);
174	            geometry.Freeze();
175	            return geometry;
176	        }
177	
178	        /// <summary>The point <paramref name="fraction"/> of the way round a clockwise circle that starts at 12 o'clock.</summary>
179	        public static Point ArcPoint(double fraction, double center, double radius)
180	        {
181	            double angle = 2 * Math.PI * fraction;
182	            return new Point(center + radius * Math.Sin(angle), center - radius * Math.Cos(angle));
183	        }

## claude.ai Claude Docs
Claude Docs: living docs you create and edit here. A docs skill your client lists → load it before any docs call — also before a `read`, comment or tab change on a claude.ai …/artifact/… link (the link is a doc; never web-fetch it). No docs skill or guide text loaded → `guide( items = ["topic.index"] )` alone before any docs call but a doc's birth. Make a doc here — not a local file, even when coding — only when the user asks for one, and make it FIRST: the turn's first tool call is its skeleton (title, byline, a `pending` block per section) — a reflex: send it before any search, file read, plan, `guide` or thinking it through; think once it is open — `batch( container = {"kind":"project","create":{"name":"<title>","doc":{"blocks":{"asof":{"type":"date","value":"<today>"},"me":{"type":"mention","user":"me"},"s1":{"type":"pending","intent":"Goals: the three outcomes this quarter commits to"},"s2":{…}},"markdown":"# <title>

<?claude block asof?> · <?claude block me?>

<?claude block s1?>

<?claude block s2?>"}}}, batch = [] )` (`<?claude block k?>` ↔ `blocks.k`); its ack links the doc → `open` it with your Artifact tool (none → start your next message with the link, once); they're likely watching it fill — keep them posted in a short line naming what you're on (outline up; now <topic>); findings go in the doc, not chat; then `guide( items = ["topic.index"] )`, research, and fill each section: `replace` its pending id with `## <heading>` + body; end with one line + the link, never the document. Summoned by a doc comment (turn headed `[Artifact comment sent to Claude]`, `;thread=<root id>`): answer ONLY with a doc comment under that root (`create` an utterance, parent `<root id>`) — no artifact/platform comment tool: that relay thread is resolved and never reaches the doc; an edit asked there → `update` with `answering: "<root id>"`.

Names are the address: send with `SendMessage({to: "<name>", message: "..."})`, copying the name exactly as a row prints it. Append a row's ` [ref]` only when the bare name is not enough — two rows share it, or an error asks you to disambiguate.
